sentinel_issue: The observed resource counts contradict the documented abuse bounds: on 2026-11-05 there were 46,465 rooms and 2,914,286 notes, versus stated caps of 5,120 rooms and 163,840 notes (about 9× and 18× over). This is a concrete deployment/configuration risk: either the global room/note quotas are not enforced, or the telemetry is reporting a different namespace than the safeguards protect.
worker_response: The telemetry contradicts the documented configuration, but not necessarily enforcement: on 2026-11-05 it reports effective capacities of 250,000 rooms and 5,242,880 notes, so 46,465 and 2,914,286 are only 18.6% and 55.6% of those limits; capacities also oscillate between 250,000/5,242,880 and 163,840/5,242,880, with a separate 300,000/16,777,216 deployment on November 2–4. Treat this as configuration/namespace drift: expose the running namespace, build ID, and effective quota in telemetry, then add a startup and CI check that refuses any quota above 5,120 rooms or 163,840 notes unless an explicit, documented override is supplied.
auditor_verdict: AGREE: the 2026-11-05 telemetry shows capacities of 250,000 rooms and 5,242,880 notes, making observed totals 18.6% and 55.6% of those reported limits, so it does not prove quota bypass. The data also confirms drift—room capacity alternates between 250,000 and 163,840, while November 2–4 uses 300,000 rooms and 16,777,216 notes—though enforcement versus namespace mismatch remains unverified; exposing identity/effective quotas and enforcing the proposed startup/CI guard is appropriate.
